findings.message: Stored passwords are now hashed with salted MD5, a fast hash that offline attackers can brute-force at billions of guesses per second. It replaces scrypt, which the docstring notes the security policy requires. Any password database leak would expose most user passwords.
findings.suggestion: return hashlib.scrypt(password.encode(), salt=salt, n=2**14, r=8, p=1)

findings.message: Changing the hash algorithm without a migration path breaks sign-in for every existing account. Their stored hashes are scrypt outputs and will never match the new MD5 digest.
This change alters password hashing behaviour but adds no test. Security-relevant authentication code needs a test that would catch it being weakened.
